paper_title: What are they talking about Benchmarking Large Language Models for   Knowledge-Grounded Discussion Summarization
caption: Paragraph retrieval ratios 0.90\% of LLMs. The majority of LLMs can be classified as either conservative (ratio<300.90{%}) or open retrievers (ratio>380.90{%}).
model_annotation: The bar chart displays the retrieval ratio (%) for various large language models, with the horizontal axis listing the model names—GPT-4o, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3 Opus, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama-3.1-405B, Mistral Large, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-Max, and GLM-4-Plus—and the vertical axis representing the retrieval ratio in percentage, scaled linearly from 0 to 50 with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each bar is color-coded and labeled with its corresponding retrieval ratio value: GPT-4o at 34.11%, GPT-4-turbo at 29.07%, GPT-4o-mini at 29.16%, Claude 3 Opus at 43.57%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet at 25.92%, Claude 3.5 Haiku at 31.56%, Gemini 1.5 Pro at 28.49%, Llama-3.1-405B at 39.37%, Mistral Large at 37.99%, DeepSeek-V3 at 31.04%, Qwen-Max at 46.94%, and GLM-4-Plus at 43.58%. The bar for Claude 3 Opus is the tallest, reaching 43.57%, while the shortest bar corresponds to Claude 3.5 Sonnet at 25.92%. The bars are arranged in the order of the model names as listed on the horizontal axis, without explicit sorting by value, and none of the bars are visually distinguished by special formatting such as shading, bolding, or annotations.
